title: Landlord Duty to Refund Security Deposit within 30 Days
content: In India, a landlord must return the tenant's security deposit within 30 days of vacating the premises under the Model Tenancy Act and state Rent Control Acts. Landlords are only permitted to deduct money for actual unpaid rent or physical damage caused by tenant negligence, backed by itemized repair bills. Landlords cannot deduct money for normal wear and tear. If a landlord unlawfully refuses to refund the deposit, the tenant has the right to file a petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal under Section 21, or issue a formal legal notice demanding refund with interest.
citation: Model Tenancy Act 2021, Section 13 & 21 (Security Deposit Refund Rights)

act_name: Protection of Women from Sexual Harassment at Workplace Act, 2013
title: Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) & POSH Complaint Timelines
content: Under the POSH Act 2013, every organization employing 10 or more employees is mandated to establish an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) headed by a senior female employee. Any aggrieved woman can submit a written complaint of workplace sexual harassment to the ICC within 3 months of the incident (extendable by another 3 months). The ICC must complete its inquiry within 90 days and submit its report within 10 days of completion. Employers must take action on the ICC recommendations within 60 days.
citation: POSH Act 2013, Section 4 & 9 (Internal Complaints Committee & Reporting Rules)

title: Consumer Rights to Redressal and E-Daakhil Filing
content: Under Section 2(9) of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, Indian consumers possess six fundamental rights: right to safety, right to information, right to choice, right to be heard, right to seek redressal, and right to consumer awareness. If a product is defective, service is deficient, or an e-commerce platform sells misleading items, consumers can file an online complaint via e-Daakhil or approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under Section 35 for replacement, full refund, or compensation without needing a lawyer.
citation: Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 2(9) & 35 (Consumer Redressal Rights)

topic: Right to Information Request & Response Timelines
title: RTI Application Rights and Mandatory 30-Day Response Limit
content: Under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act 2005, any Indian citizen can request public information from any government department or public authority by submitting an application to the Public Information Officer (PIO). Under Section 7(1), the PIO must provide the requested information within 30 days of receiving the application. If the information concerns the life or liberty of a person, the PIO must respond within 48 hours. If the PIO fails to respond or refuses unlawfully, the citizen can file a First Appeal within 30 days under Section 19(1).

title: 26 Weeks Paid Maternity Leave & Mandatory Workplace Creche
content: The Maternity Benefit Act entitles female employees in establishments with 10 or more employees to 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave for their first two children. Under Section 11A, establishments with 50 or more employees are required to provide a creche facility within a prescribed distance. Employers are strictly prohibited from terminating or dismissing a woman from service during or on account of her maternity leave.
citation: Maternity Benefit Act 2017, Section 5 & 11A (Paid Maternity Leave & Creche Rules)

act_name: Code on Wages, 2019 / Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
title: Gender Non-Discrimination in Wages & Minimum Wage Guarantee
content: Under the Code on Wages 2019 and Equal Remuneration Act, employers cannot discriminate between male and female employees regarding wages for the same work or work of similar nature. Every worker is legally entitled to receive minimum wages fixed by the appropriate government, timely payment of wages on or before the 7th day of the month, and safe working conditions.
citation: Code on Wages 2019, Section 3 & 4 (Equal Pay & Minimum Wage Protection)

title: Eligibility for Free Legal Aid via NALSA / DLSA
content: Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, free legal services (including legal representation by advocates, court fee payment, and document preparation) are guaranteed to women, children, members of Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, industrial workmen, persons in custody, and individuals whose annual income does not exceed the state prescribed limit. Citizens can apply directly to the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or State Legal Services Authority (SALSA).
citation: Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, Section 12 (Free Legal Aid Rights)

title: Right to Grounds of Arrest, Legal Counsel, and 24-Hour Magistrate Production
content: Under Article 22(1) of the Indian Constitution and Section 50 of CrPC, every person arrested by police has the right to be informed immediately of the grounds of arrest, the right to inform a family member or friend, and the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice. Under Article 22(2), the arrested individual must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time). For bailable offenses, police are legally bound to inform the arrested person of their right to bail.
citation: Constitution of India Art. 22 & CrPC Sec. 50 (Arrest Safeguards & 24hr Rule)
